observation.visible_scene: An underwater shot in greenish-tinted seawater. For the first half the frame is filled by a coral/rock reef wall encrusted with algae, around which a school of small striped fish (sergeant-major type) and a few darker fish swim; a thin pale vertical line hangs in the lower-centre of the reef view. As the clip progresses the view opens onto the water surface and the sky: a snorkeler wearing a mask and dark trunks appears near the surface, and the camera ends pointed straight up at the surface, showing a bright circular 'window' of sun and blue sky surrounded by the mirror-like, totally-reflecting water surface, with fish silhouetted against it.
visible_changes: The camera continuously pitches/tilts upward: the reef, which fills the frame at t=0, slides down and out of view by about t=1.4s, while the water surface and sky rise from the top to fill the whole frame.

A snorkeler first becomes visible at the top edge around t=1.0s (torso/legs), then appears more fully (masked head, outstretched arms) centred near the surface from t=1.07s to t=1.4s; as the camera keeps tilting up, the diver drifts toward the bottom edge (head at bottom in t=1.47s, body at bottom-centre in t=2.67s) rather than moving through the water independently.
The thin vertical line seen in the lower-centre of the reef view is present throughout the first ~0.9s and is no longer in frame once the camera points up.
Throughout, individual striped and small fish change position and orientation, swimming relative to both the reef (early) and the surface/sky (late); their motion is independent of the camera tilt.
The bright sun disc grows and centres within the circular surface window as the upward tilt completes (most prominent from t=1.6s onward).
outside_clip_unknowns: The diver's entry into the scene and any action before t=0 are not shown; the clip begins mid-view on the reef and ends mid-view on the surface, so neither endpoint is a start or stop of the tilt.
Whether the camera is held by the snorkeler or by a separate operator, and the true nature of the thin vertical line, cannot be determined from these frames.
uncertain_details: Exact direction and speed of the snorkeler's own swimming is hard to separate from the camera's upward rotation; the diver appears roughly stationary relative to the surface while the frame tilts.
Some fish near the bright surface may be reflections/silhouettes rather than distinct individuals at that depth.
